title: Tenant egress metadata mispairing after GPU pool resize causes transient cross-tenant DNS rebinding
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS resolution where tenant A started receiving DNS responses that belonged to tenant B after large GPU pool resizes. The issue manifests as short-lived hostname rebinding and stale egress metadata mapping leading to connection failures and certificate mismatches for TLS handshakes in hosted endpoints. This ticket tracks the investigation, fixes, and rollout for a production patch to prevent metadata mispairing during autoscaler-driven pod migrations.
customer_reports: 2026-02-24: ACME Chat - multiple 5xx errors and hostname mismatch alerts after scheduled scale event
2026-02-25: FinLens Analytics - session creation failures and intermittent auth failures correlated with node replacement
impact_summary: High customer impact: P0. Affected customers saw request failures, TLS hostname mismatch alerts, and short periods of cross-tenant DNS responses lasting 10-90 seconds during aggressive GPU pool scaling. Incident occurred in two regions; not all tenants reproducible.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a Dedicated GPU pool with multiple tenant assignments and enable aggressive scale down to simulate removal of hosts.
2) Trigger a rapid scale-down then scale-up of the GPU pool to force pod evictions and rebind onto different compute hosts.
3) While rebinds occur, repeatedly resolve tenant-scoped hostnames from a tenant pod that is being migrated.
4) Observe transient DNS responses containing A/AAAA records that resolve to IPs owned by a different tenant when metadata mapping updates were delayed.
5) Observe TLS client logs showing hostname verification failures when IPs reuse old egress metadata.
Notes: Repro requires load on resolver caches and low DNS TTLs to amplify window.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-26 - Initial triage: Spike in customer tickets during scheduled autoscaler runs. Collected packet captures and resolver logs.
2026-02-27 - Correlated incidents with GPU pool resize jobs; saw metadata update races in the egress mapping service when nodes were drained and reattached.

2026-02-28 - Root cause hypothesis: egress metadata (tenant_id -> interface_id mapping) updated non-atomically across control-plane caches. During aggressive reallocation, some request routing paths used stale mapping while others used updated mapping, causing DNS reply multiplexing to be associated with the wrong tenant context.
2026-03-02 - Confirmed that resolver cache TTLs plus delayed atomic swap of 'egress-assignment' protobuf produced a 10-90s window where remote resolvers returned IPs that had been reassigned.
2026-03-04 - Created a small repro harness to accelerate route reassignment and validate fix hypotheses.

2026-03-06 - Implemented a fix branch that introduces a versioned assignment token and a reconciliation checkpoint to ensure mapping updates are visible to all control-plane slices before node egress is accepted.
2026-03-09 - Ran canary against 3 dedicated pools in staging with synthetic tenants; DNS rebinding window eliminated in 50+ runs.
2026-03-11 - Added defensive TTL clamp behavior for tenant-hosted records and tightened metrics around mapping-update-latency for future alerting.
2026-03-12 - Security review requested because change touches tenant isolation paths; sec team confirmed approach with two minor recommendations (audit log changes + KMS-backed signing for token).
decisions: Adopt versioned egress-assignment tokens to make mapping updates atomic across control-plane replicas.
Introduce a short control-plane gating window: new assignment tokens must be published and observed by >=2 control-plane replicas before traffic is accepted on reattached egress interfaces.
Clamp DNS TTL to a minimum of 5s for tenant-scoped records during active reassignment windows to reduce cache amplification.
Add a reconciliation worker that periodically verifies assignments and repairs mismatches within 30s.
Require a security audit and signature on assignment tokens; integrate KMS signing in this release.
fix_notes: PR #rwinf/egress-assign: added token version, publish/observe handshake, and reconciliation worker
PR #rwinf/dns-agent: TTL-clamp and per-tenant audit logging for assignment swaps
PR #infra/agent-deploy: deployment hooks to wait for assignment token propagation before enabling egress
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs into release branch runtime-1.23-rc
2) Deploy to staging and run repro harness (50+ runs) - verify no rebinding windows
3) Canary: deploy to two small Dedicated pools in us-west-2 with monitoring guards
4) Monitor mapping-update-latency and DNS-rebind-alert for 72h; if stable, expand to 20% of Dedicated pools
5) Full rollout across Dedicated after 7 days of stable canary metrics
Rollback: rollback infra hook to block egress activation if handshake not observed by >=2 replicas
testing_plan: Unit tests for token handshake in egress-assign (CI)
Integration test: simulated multi-replica control plane publish/observe race
E2E: repro harness that scales GPU pools aggressively in staging and checks for cross-tenant DNS responses
Dogfood run on non-customer Dedicated pools overnight before canary
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: dns_rebind_detected (cross-tenant A/AAAA mismatch) -> Pager + automated rollback
Dashboard: per-pool mapping-update-latency, canary pass rate, TLS hostname-verify-failures
follow_up_tasks: Postmortem and customer communication: draft RCA + mitigation summary for ACME and FinLens
Extend reconciliation worker to cover peering/overlay VNI assignment edge cases
Add e2e chaos test for node drain + immediate reattach to catch future regressions
Consider stronger invariants: KVS transactions for assignment metadata in future cycle
resolution_summary: Patch introduces a versioned assignment token and control-plane publish/observe handshake, plus a reconciliation worker and DNS TTL clamp. Staging canaries show elimination of the rebinding window. Security team approved with minor audit logging changes. Preparing customer-facing RCA and rolling to production via runtime-1.23 rollout.
